item.title: Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
item.description:
Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the Middle East conflict.

The Gulf kingdom has suffered several attacks this week, ending a weeks-long lull in the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

item.title: In an Egypt village, generations of Palestinians denied a normal life
item.description:
Shamma Abu Hussein is possibly the last person in her village of refugees to have lived in historic Palestine. Living in Egypt, she has watched three generations of her family grow up in legal limbo.

She was among the hundreds of thousands who fled or were expelled during the creation of the State of Israel in 1948, whose descendants number in the millions.

Now she fears that the effects of the Gaza war and rhetoric from Israeli ministers calling for Gazans to be expelled means history is repeating itself.

item.title: Syrian Christian town demands security after resident kidnapped
item.description:
When Amina saw her nephew's motorbike knocked onto the ground and a car speeding away from his home in central Syria, she thought there had been a crash.

Instead, 38-year-old jeweller Maher Sankari had been kidnapped, an incident that plunged the Christian town of Suqaylabiyah into fear and prompted church leaders to demand authorities take action against repeated attacks and kidnappings of Christians.

Sankari's captors are demanding an eye-watering ransom of 120 kilogrammes (265 pounds) of gold.

item.title: COP31 climate talks close to final deal, says summit president
item.description:
By Tuvan Gumrukcu and Ali Kucukgocmen

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) - UN climate talks in Turkey approached a final deal on Sunday with the announcement of a new package that COP31 presidents Australia and Turkey hope will achieve consensus on how to advance the fight against global warming.

The new draft deal was released two days after the conference in Antalya was scheduled to end.

item.title: US denies Iranian account that missile damaged F-16 over Gulf
item.description:
Nov 21 (Reuters) - US Central Command on Saturday denied an Iranian account that its forces had fired a missile at a US F-16 fighter jet over the Gulf, damaging the aircraft and forcing it to make an emergency landing.

Iranian state media earlier reported that the country's air defence systems targeted the aircraft on Friday evening, causing it to abort its mission and land at a nearby airport.

item.title: UK man swims in Strait of Hormuz to highlight environmental damage
item.description:
A British endurance swimmer who swam in waters in the Strait of Hormuz to highlight the "devastating environmental consequences of war" on Saturday called for the waterway to be reopened and the pollution in it to be cleaned up.

"Oil tankers, gas carriers and other merchant ships are being attacked, day after day. The environmental consequences of this war will last for generations," Lewis Pugh wrote in a post on his website.

item.title: Israeli strike on vehicle in Gaza kills three, Gaza Health Ministry says
item.description:
JERUSALEM, Nov 21 (Reuters) - Israeli forces hit a truck in Gaza on Saturday which witnesses said was carrying food and papers bearing the logo of the World Central Kitchen charity, but the organisation said the vehicle was not affiliated with it.

The Gaza Health Ministry said three people were killed in the incident in Gaza City.

The Israeli military said its forces had been targeting Islamic Jihad militants in the area at the time and that the vehicle had been transporting food to members of the organisation.

item.title: COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime
item.description:
By Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The COP31 climate summit will either produce a good deal or no deal at all, the European Union's top climate official said on Saturday as talks stretched deep into overtime.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, delaying an agreement at the two-week conference that had been scheduled to end on Friday.

item.title: Gaza civil defence says Israeli fire kills four
item.description:
Gaza's civil defence told AFP that Israeli fire killed four people on Saturday, including three in a strike on a vehicle carrying food aid in the war-ravaged territory.

The Israeli military said it had struck "three terrorists from the military wing" of Islamic Jihad who had been travelling in a van carrying food and supplies for the militant group allied with Hamas.

item.title: Fire at power station in Iraq's Basra kills at least 4, injures 35
item.description:
BASRA, Iraq, Nov 21 (Reuters) - At least 4 people were killed and 35 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.

Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.

The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.

item.title: Araqchi says Iran wants diplomacy to end war, Trump says terms unacceptable
item.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran still hoped diplomacy could end its war with the United States, while US President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but one that wasnot acceptable to him.

Araqchi told the state-owned Iran newspaper that messages continued to be exchanged between Iran and Washington through mediators, and that Tehran was seeking "an agreement that would ensure there was no further war".

item.title: US Vice President Vance declines to say he would have ordered Iran strikes
item.description:
By Bo Erickson and Jacob Bogage

WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US Vice President JD Vance on Friday declined to say whether he would have authorized strikes on Iran to prevent the country from developing a nuclear weapon, sidestepping President Donald Trump's calls for him to say the attacks were necessary and that he would carry them out again.

Speaking at a White House press conference alongside Trump, Vance said the decision to attack Iran in February was Trump's call, "and my job is to support the president of the United States."

item.title: European emissions proposal faces Middle East pushback at UN aviation agency
item.description:
By Allison Lampert

MONTREAL, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Plans to change the European Union's Emissions Trading System faced pushback at a global aviation gathering that wraps up on Friday, as Middle East countries challenged fresh efforts to curb pollution from airlines outside an existing deal.

item.title: Trump cites good talks with Putin on Ukraine, holds back on security guarantees
item.description:
By Bo Erickson and Doina Chiacu

WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he and Russian leader Vladimir Putin held very good talks on Ukraine during their meeting in China, but added he didn't want to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine without a broader peace deal.

"We're having very good talks. I think there's a real good chance that we can get it done," Trump said at a White House press conference after his trip to Asia, where he met Putin and Chinese President XiJinping.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
item.description:
Yemen's Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday, after vowing reprisals for a "special operation" by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.

Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.

An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat".

item.title: US ‘would welcome’ UN leader from Latin America, says Waltz amid gridlock
item.description: Former UAE ambassador to the United Nations Lana Nusseibeh jumped to third in Friday’s straw poll while still receiving three "discourage" votes from permanent security council members.

item.title: How war shifted Iran's missile ambitions beyond the Middle East
item.description: The conflict has battered Iran's military capabilities, but the leadership appears to have drawn the lesson that deterrence must reach further and inflict greater costs.
